title: Cuphead: Baroness Von Bon Bon: theatrical facial extremes

people.name: Tina Nawrocki
people.role: Animator and designer of this character, identified in her own production post

summary: Closed eyes, an open jaw, a clenched grin and startled eyes demonstrate distinct emotional drawings.

observations.text: The compact pose combines closed eyelids with a tiny heart-like mouth. Another drawing expands the jaw and makes the two eyes unequal.
The detached-head drawing uses inward-angled lids and a broad toothy mouth. Spiral hair and the conical hat preserve identity.
The leaning drawing opens both eyes while keeping the mouth small. Face and extended arms jointly establish the reaction.

mistIdeas: Our inference: approve an expression sheet with distinct mouth and lid drawings before interpolating motion.
Our inference: support a readable facial reaction with a small head movement rather than animating every feature constantly.

title: Pizza Tower: Peppino's elastic expression shapes

people.name: Pizza Tower Guy (McPig)
people.role: Programming and animations, self-described in the 2019 developer interview

summary: A useful upper limit for expression amplitude: the face changes silhouette as well as internal eye and mouth shapes.

observations.text: The three-pose Peppino illustration contrasts a huge horizontal tooth-and-mouth opening with a tiny puckered mouth. The eyes protrude beyond the head mass and shift together toward the object of attention.

The creator says his drawing approach lets him animate quickly without keeping identical proportions in every drawing. This supports controlled proportion changes, but does not establish a particular frame count or timing curve.

mistIdeas: Our inference: make a surprised MIST pose change the spacing and height of both eyes before adding extra effects. Let the silhouette carry the reaction.
Our inference: reserve a short eye-shape overshoot for exceptional surprise, then recover to MIST's normal proportions. Preserve its own face design and palette.
Our inference: test a tiny compressed mouth against a much wider peak mouth. These distinct key poses may read better than several subtly different smiles.

observations.text: In the inspected close-up, Stella's pupils point upward and left, her mouth forms a small closed smile, and her arms enclose Daffodil. The face and protective gesture carry the same gentle attitude.
The creators attribute the trailer's emotional effect to small facial changes and body language, supported by color, lighting, music and timing.

mistIdeas: Our inference: test a quiet contentment state with a small mouth curve, stable upward gaze and a modest head angle. Keep ample space between this and a delighted grin.
Our inference: preserve an emotional eye-and-brow pose across talking mouth shapes. The still suggests this separation as a design approach; it does not prove the trailer uses such a rig.

title: Dory prototype - independent eye and mouth controls

people.name: Chris (twocentstudios)
people.role: Solo developer and author of the Dory character prototype

summary: A small, unusually explicit prototype shows how graphic facial shapes can remain independent of body animation.

observations.text: The author models separate open and closed eye objects, parents them to the character's armature, and tests blink control with the action button.
He proposes named expressions pairing eye and mouth shapes, driven from dialogue; his working blink demo uses a separate Godot AnimationPlayer so body animation can continue.

mistIdeas: Our inference: keep expression choice, gaze, blink and speech-mouth controllers separate, with clear priorities when they overlap.
Our inference: prototype an emotional pose using a small set of deliberate shapes before adding continuous morphs. Independence should permit a listening mouth to remain still while the eyes react.

title: Astro Bot: LED eyes and physical acting

people.name: Jamie Alexander Smith
people.role: Animation Lead, Astro Bot Rescue Mission

people.name: Jamie Smith
people.role: Principal Animation Director, Team Asobi (2024 interview)

people.name: Sebastian Brueckner
people.role: Art Director, Astro Bot Rescue Mission

summary: A directly relevant screen-face reference with named animation staff and original studio-published GIFs.

observations.text: Doucet says the design deliberately avoided a mouth and stretching faces, leaving the eyes as its main expressive feature.

The inspected celebration GIF frame combines two upward blue eye arcs with lifted hands and an upright body. The face has no separately drawn pupil, brow or mouth; the silhouette reinforces the eye expression.

The Rescue Mission team reports that conventional cartoon exaggeration required timing adjustments for VR. They also describe bosses becoming vulnerable and silly as the player hits back, making expression a response to progress in the encounter.
Jamie Smith describes studying children's excited actions, including jumping, to build playfulness into animation.

mistIdeas: Our inference: test a small eye-shape vocabulary on MIST's existing face before adding extra facial features. Pair each shape with one readable head or body attitude.
Our inference: make a completed action trigger a held pleased shape, followed by a small recovery. Do not run the entire expressive vocabulary as an idle loop.
Our inference: use a blink at a change of attention or after a completed reaction, then let the new gaze settle. This is a proposed MIST experiment, not a verified Astro blink rule.
